newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB SAYS SETS AUG DEBENTURE COUPON AT 2.55 PCT.
newsitem.headline: NCB SAYS SETS AUG DEBENTURE COUPON AT 2.55 PCT.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Tuesday it would leave the coupon rate for its August five-year bank debenture unchanged from the previous month at 2.55 percent.
NCB also said it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for August at 2.7 percent, unchanged from July.
The spread between the coupon rate of the Industrial Bank of Japan's (IBJ) five-year bank debenture and NCB's debenture is now 0.75 percentage point, unchanged since February.
Traders said there have not been any bids or offers recently for NCB's July five-year debentures with a coupon rate of 2.55 percent.
The long-term prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year or more to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
Japan's three long-term credit banks customarily set their prime rates 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of IBJ's five-year debenture, which is the benchmark in the debenture market.

IBJ said on Monday it would leave its long-term prime rate for August unchanged from July at 2.7 percent. It also said it would leave the coupon rate for its August debenture unchanged at 1.8 percent.
